title: Colombian President thanks US $1 billion support
seoTitle: Colombian President Thanks US $1 Billion Support
subtitle: Package includes technology, narcotrafficking combat and economic investments
excerpt: On August 10, 2026, Colombia's president warmly welcomed the U.S. pledge of $1 billion to strengthen security and fight narcotrafficking.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On August 10, 2026, Colombian President Abelardo De La Espriella expressed deep satisfaction upon receiving the news of a $1 billion security package announced by the United States. The measure, initially disclosed on August 7, aims to strengthen cooperation in security, combat narcotrafficking, and economic development.

Reaction of the Colombian president

De La Espriella described the support as a backing of special importance for the bilateral relationship, stating that it confirms Colombia's position as a reliable and strategic ally of the U.S. The Presidency's statement highlighted that the announcement shows Colombia has regained its place in the world.

Details of the security package

The agreement provides for Colombia's incorporation into the Shield of the Americas and the strengthening of security forces through American technology. It also includes an expansion of coca eradication and cocaine interception operations, as well as actions to dismantle criminal organizations through asset freezing and prosecution of financiers.

Actions against narcotrafficking and armed groups

The plan includes the recovery of territories controlled by armed groups and the protection of minors from forced recruitment. The new agenda emphasizes enhancing interoperability between the forces of both countries and developing coordinated operations against transnational terrorist and criminal organizations.

Economic and infrastructure components

An economic component will be developed through bilateral dialogue, covering economic stabilization, investment in critical minerals, and support for Colombian small and medium enterprises. Cooperation also includes modernization of digital, port, and energy infrastructure, as well as collaboration on civilian nuclear energy for peaceful purposes.

Outlook for the bilateral relationship

Congressman Mario Díaz-Balart highlighted that the package demonstrates firm U.S. support for its allies, reinforcing the shared fight against narco‑terrorism and advancing mutual national interests. The State Department announced the initiative during De La Espriella's inauguration, sending a delegation led by interim Attorney General Todd Blanche. While the resources still depend on approval by the U.S. Congress, the Colombian Presidency considers the backing the most important support received in decades.

With information from El Tiempo.
